hero.caption: Santo António Church or Chapel. Ilha de Mozambique was first occupied by Portuguese explorers in the late 1400s. They quickly estblished a fort there, and with time quite a community sprang up, including a church, mosque, shops, and residences. This church is one of the architectural remains there. The island, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is off the eastern coast of Africa and is part of the country of Mozambique.

images.caption:
Site of the Massacre of Mueda on June 16, 1960, when Portuguese troops fired on a demonstration claiming independence from Portugal, and threw some demonstrators into a ravine.[1] Resentment generated by these events led ultimately to independentist guerrilla FRELIMO gaining needed momentum in the outset of the Mozambican War of Independence (1964-1975). 

Image was taken with 35mm camera and scanned with Nikon Coolscan V ED.
